passage: On the tram in Rotterdam, Tuan checked his phone for the third time in ten minutes. Across from him sat Tomas, an old friend visiting for the weekend, halfway through a story about his mother's illness. Tuan's thumb scrolled without reading. His stomach felt tight; he was waiting for a message about his own job contract and could not concentrate. Tomas trailed off. "Am I boring you?" he asked, and Tuan flushed. He put the phone away. "No. I am sorry. I am waiting for news on my contract and my hands keep reaching for it. Your mother matters. Please, go on." Tomas nodded, and this time the story was heard properly.

qa.q: What was Tomas talking about when Tuan checked his phone?
qa.a: Tomas was talking about his mother's illness.

qa.q: Why did Tuan keep reaching for his phone, and how did Tomas read it?
qa.a: Tuan was anxious about his contract and could not concentrate, and Tomas read it as boredom. Both readings were possible until Tuan explained.
Tuan put the phone away, explained what he was waiting for and asked Tomas to go on.

qa.q: How might Tomas have felt when Tuan scrolled during his story?
qa.a: He probably felt unimportant or hurt, since he trailed off and asked if he was boring Tuan.

grounding: Third-person narrative set abroad about a young adult fiddling with a phone from anxiety, read as disrespect, resolved by a short explanation.

passage: Community centre meeting notes, as I saw them. During Madhav's presentation on the new library timings, Darshan kept looking at his phone under the table, tapping, scrolling, locking the screen, unlocking it again. Madhav faltered and looked at the floor. After the meeting I asked Darshan what was going on. He said, "My sister's exam results were due and I could not sit still. I should have said so." He then went to Madhav and explained. Madhav said, "I thought I was losing you." They both laughed a little. Nobody can tell from the tapping alone whether someone is bored, anxious or dealing with something urgent.

qa.a: He was presenting the new library timings.

qa.q: What was Darshan probably feeling while tapping the phone, and what did Madhav think it meant?
qa.a: It came from worry about his sister's exam results, and Madhav read it as losing his audience. This shows the same habit can look like disrespect when it is anxiety.

qa.q: What could Darshan have done to prevent the misunderstanding?
qa.a: He could have quietly said before the meeting that he was waiting for urgent news, or stepped out to check his phone.

qa.q: How might Madhav have felt during the presentation?
qa.a: He probably felt discouraged and unsure, since he faltered and looked at the floor when Darshan kept checking the phone.

grounding: Institutional scene of a young adult fiddling with a phone from worry, read as disrespect, cleared up by a short explanation.
